name: Escape hatches
tagline: any, casts, and optional fields that are never really optional
notes: stop using `any` for the order payload
that `as Order` cast hides a missing field
`shippedAt` is optional but it is always set once status is shipped
you added another `as unknown as` to make the compiler quiet
don't reach for `any` again, type the status properly
pattern: Illegal states are representable, so the agent keeps reaching for `any`, casts, and optional fields to paper over them.
wrongFix: Remember to avoid `any` and casts. Don't forget that shippedAt is always set when an order is shipped.

fix.title: Model the order as a discriminated union and delete the cast
fix.summary: Each status carries exactly the fields it has. A shipped order without `shippedAt` no longer type-checks, so there is nothing to cast around.
fix.whyNotWeaker: A lint rule banning `any` would still let `as Order` through, and a runtime check only fires after the bad object exists. The type removes the state.

before.caption: Leaky: one bag of optionals, held together by a cast
lines: const order = payload as any as Order

after.caption: Encoded: the bad state cannot be written down

name: Validate later
tagline: guards scattered through the middle of the code
notes: remember to validate the payload before using it
that bug was unparsed JSON again
check the API response before use
the webhook body was trusted without validation
you forgot to validate the query params in the handler
pattern: Validation lives in the middle of the code, so every new call site has to remember to re-check data that should already be trusted.
wrongFix: Remember to validate the payload and check the API response before you use it.

fix.title: Parse at the boundary; inside, only parsed types exist
fix.summary: One `parseChargeEvent` runs where data enters (route, webhook, fetch). It returns a typed value or a 400. Internal functions accept only the parsed type, so unparsed JSON cannot reach them.
fix.whyNotWeaker: A shared `validate()` helper still has to be remembered at every call site, and scattered runtime checks keep the guard in the middle. Moving the parse to the edge makes raw input unrepresentable inside.

before.caption: Leaky: raw JSON flows in, guards sprinkled later
lines: const body = await req.json() // unknown, used as-is
if (!body?.amount) return // remembered here, not elsewhere

after.caption: Encoded: one parse at the edge, typed everywhere after
lines: async function charge(e: ChargeEvent) { /* no guards needed */ }

name: Banned call
tagline: a rule that only exists as a sentence
notes: don't call `fs` from the route handler
stop shelling out there with child_process
that API is banned in app code
you imported `fs` into a page component again
no `exec` in request handlers, use the job queue
pattern: The rule only exists as a sentence, so it is re-broken every time the agent edits a route or page.
wrongFix: Don't forget: never call fs or child_process from app code. Use the job queue instead.

fix.title: Ban the import in app code and fail CI
fix.summary: An ESLint `no-restricted-imports` rule scoped to `src/app/**` rejects `fs`, `node:fs`, and `child_process` with a message pointing at the queue. The build goes red before review.
fix.whyNotWeaker: No type can stop an import, so the strongest fit is a check. A runtime guard would only fire in production, and a helper is optional. Lint fails the build on every edit.

before.caption: Leaky: the rule is a comment
lines: // NOTE: please don't use fs in routes

after.caption: Encoded: the build refuses it
lines: message: "Enqueue a job via lib/jobs instead."
// $ bun run lint  ->  error  'fs' import is restricted

name: Nil-check bandage
tagline: silence the crash, keep the cause
notes: just add a null check so it stops crashing
you swallowed the crash with try/catch again
guard it so the page doesn't blow up
another `user?.profile?.name ?? ''` fallback hiding a missing profile
the undefined comes from getProfile, not from the page
pattern: The symptom is silenced at each call site while the producer keeps returning a missing value.
wrongFix: Just add a null check there, and remember to guard user.profile anywhere it is used.

fix.title: Fix the producer: return a Profile or an explicit NotFound
fix.summary: `getProfile` returns `{ kind: "found", profile } | { kind: "missing" }`. Callers must handle both cases once, and a found profile always has a name. The `?.` chains go away.
fix.whyNotWeaker: Another null check is a runtime bandage at one call site; the next caller crashes again. Changing what the producer can return removes the hole for every caller.
